sources.title: Reproducible processed-event, outbox and retry state-model test

claims.text: Kafka producer documentation states that enable.idempotence prevents producer-retry duplicates and that transactional.id implies idempotence and transaction recovery semantics. The replacement candidate explicitly limits this guarantee to Kafka transport rather than extending it to external databases or HTTP side effects.
Kafka consumer documentation defines read_committed so consumers return only committed transactional records and respect the last stable offset boundary while transactions are in flight.

Kafka delivery-semantics documentation explains that exactly-once interaction with external destinations requires cooperation with the destination storage system. The candidate therefore uses one local database transaction for processed-event state, business state, and outbox, then advances the consumer offset after that transaction commits.

The executable state model verifies that duplicate delivery after an uncommitted offset does not create a second business or outbox result and that an ambiguous relay retry preserves the same downstream event ID. The candidate makes production correctness conditional on real database transaction/unique-constraint semantics and downstream idempotency.

The replacement candidate declares throughput and latency assumptions, concrete processed-event/business/outbox state, duplicate and crash recovery, ambiguous-send handling, long-failure compensation, observability and failure-injection acceptance tests. These are presented as design requirements to validate, not as measured production claims.

findings: 场景假设缺少端到端 SLO/业务规模或待澄清验收目标。
